incident_a.first_symptom: 2024-03-15T14:08:44+00:00 - API gateway observed elevated p99 request latency (340ms vs 120ms baseline), indicating downstream degradation
incident_a.impact_moment: 2024-03-15T14:11:10+00:00 - Trading platform halted, unable to serve price quotes to users
incident_a.resolution_trigger: Killing the long-running query q_4489 (731s duration) on user_positions table released database connection pool resources, allowing dependent services to recover

timeline.event: API gateway operating normally with p99 latency at 120ms baseline
timeline.causal_significance: Establishes healthy baseline performance metrics before incident onset

timeline.event: API gateway p99 latency increased to 340ms (283% of baseline)
timeline.causal_significance: First observable symptom indicating downstream service degradation, likely caused by database contention that had already begun

timeline.event: Pricing service detected slow query q_4821 taking 2100ms
timeline.causal_significance: Database contention manifests as slow queries in pricing service, directly contributing to elevated API gateway latency

timeline.event: Pricing service detected another slow query q_4822 taking 3400ms
timeline.causal_significance: Escalating query durations indicate worsening database contention, consuming more connection pool resources

timeline.event: Database connection pool exhausted (100 connections, 47 waiting)
timeline.causal_significance: Connection pool saturation prevents new queries from executing, causing cascading timeouts in dependent services

timeline.event: API gateway reports upstream timeout to pricing-service (5000ms)
timeline.causal_significance: Direct consequence of database pool exhaustion; pricing service cannot obtain connections to serve requests

timeline.event: Circuit breaker opened for pricing-service
timeline.causal_significance: Repeated timeout failures trigger circuit breaker, stopping all requests to pricing service to prevent further resource exhaustion

timeline.event: Trading halted - platform unable to serve price quotes
timeline.causal_significance: Circuit breaker on pricing service prevents price quote generation, forcing business-critical trading operations to halt

timeline.event: PagerDuty alert triggered, on-call engineer notified
timeline.causal_significance: Critical platform outage triggers incident response process

timeline.event: Engineer acknowledged alert and began investigation
timeline.causal_significance: Human intervention begins to diagnose and resolve root cause

timeline.event: Long-running query q_4489 killed after 731 seconds on user_positions table
timeline.causal_significance: Terminating the pathological query immediately releases held database connections, allowing pool to begin recovery

timeline.event: Database connection pool recovering, waiting queue reduced to 12
timeline.causal_significance: Released connections allow queued requests to proceed, reducing backlog from 47 to 12

timeline.event: Pricing service query latency returning to normal
timeline.causal_significance: Available database connections restore pricing service query performance to acceptable levels

timeline.event: Circuit breaker transitioned to HALF-OPEN state
timeline.causal_significance: Circuit breaker begins testing whether pricing service has recovered by allowing limited requests

timeline.event: Circuit breaker closed, service fully recovered
timeline.causal_significance: Successful test requests confirm pricing service health, restoring full traffic flow

timeline.event: Trading operations resumed
timeline.causal_significance: Full system recovery allows business-critical trading functionality to restart

timeline.event: Root cause identified: query q_4489 from scheduled batch job user_positions_recalc (runs daily at 14:00 UTC)
timeline.causal_significance: Post-incident analysis reveals the pathological query originated from a scheduled batch job that conflicted with production traffic

timeline.event: Deep root cause identified: user_positions table missing index on user_id and position_date, causing full table scan
timeline.causal_significance: Missing database index forced expensive full table scan, explaining why the batch job query consumed excessive resources and held connections for 731 seconds

incident_b.first_symptom: 2024-04-05T09:44:22+00:00 - Slow DB query detected (query_id=q_9031, duration=1800ms), first observable signal of database performance degradation
incident_b.impact_moment: 2024-04-05T09:45:40+00:00 - Order submission halted, marking complete loss of core business capability
incident_b.resolution_trigger: Killing the long-running query q_9031 that had been blocking database connections for 748 seconds, which immediately allowed connection pool recovery

timeline.event: Slow database query q_9031 detected with 1800ms duration in order-service
timeline.causal_significance: This query, originating from the daily open_orders_settlement batch job scheduled at 09:30 UTC, began consuming database resources. The query performed a full table scan on open_orders due to missing indexes on account_id and order_date columns, causing it to hold connections and locks far longer than normal queries.

timeline.event: Database connection pool exhausted with all 100 connections occupied and 39 requests waiting
timeline.causal_significance: The long-running query q_9031 held database connections open while performing the full table scan, preventing connection recycling. As the query continued to run, it starved other services of available connections, creating a cascading resource exhaustion that blocked all database-dependent operations.

timeline.event: API gateway experienced upstream timeout when calling order-service
timeline.causal_significance: Order-service could not acquire database connections due to pool exhaustion, causing requests to hang until timeout. This propagated the database-layer failure up to the API gateway, beginning user-facing degradation.

timeline.event: Circuit breaker opened for order-service at API gateway
timeline.causal_significance: Repeated timeout failures from order-service triggered the circuit breaker protection mechanism, causing the gateway to stop forwarding requests to order-service entirely. This prevented further resource waste but also blocked all order-related functionality from reaching the backend.

timeline.event: Order submission functionality completely halted
timeline.causal_significance: The combination of circuit breaker activation and continued database unavailability resulted in total loss of order submission capability, representing full business impact and the critical severity threshold of the incident.

timeline.event: Long-running query q_9031 forcibly killed after running for 748 seconds on open_orders table
timeline.causal_significance: Terminating the pathological query immediately released the database connections and locks it had been holding. This was the direct remediation action that broke the resource exhaustion cycle and enabled recovery.

timeline.event: Database connection pool began recovering
timeline.causal_significance: With query q_9031 terminated, connections were released back to the pool and became available for normal operations. The 39 waiting requests could now be serviced, allowing order-service to resume database operations.

timeline.event: Order submission functionality fully resumed
timeline.causal_significance: With database connectivity restored, order-service health checks passed, causing the circuit breaker to close and API gateway to resume forwarding traffic. This marks complete recovery of business functionality.

timeline.event: Root cause identified: query q_9031 originated from daily batch job open_orders_settlement scheduled at 09:30 UTC
timeline.causal_significance: Post-incident analysis revealed the problematic query was part of scheduled batch processing running during business hours, explaining the timing and recurrence risk of the incident pattern.

timeline.event: Root cause identified: open_orders table missing composite index on account_id and order_date columns
timeline.causal_significance: The missing index forced the batch query to perform a full table scan, explaining why query q_9031 took 748 seconds instead of milliseconds. This structural database design issue was the fundamental cause enabling the incident to occur.
